response.title: I rent and can't drill into the walls. What kind of projector screen can I use that still looks good with the lights on?
response.answer:
For a rental where you can't drill into the walls and want a projector screen that still looks good with the lights on, I'd recommend a freestanding ambient light rejecting (ALR) screen.

The key is getting both the right screen material and the right mounting style. A normal white projector screen can look washed out in a bright room, even with an expensive projector.

The 3 best renter-friendly options
Shop

1. Floor-rising ALR screen

Best overall

A motorized screen rises from a case on the floor or a low TV console. No drilling, clean appearance, and easy to hide when not in use.

Trade-off: More expensive, and the screen material must match your projector type.

Shop

2. Freestanding fixed-frame ALR screen

A rigid screen supported by floor stands, without wall mounting. Usually provides a very flat surface and can offer excellent picture quality.

Trade-off: Takes up permanent floor space and is harder to move.

Shop

3. Portable tripod or pull-up screen

Easy to move and store, with relatively affordable options.

Trade-off: Most inexpensive versions use ordinary white or gray material rather than effective ALR material, so they'll look worse with lights on.

The important part: ALR isn't all the same

Ultra-short-throw (UST) projector: Look for a UST ALR / CLR screen, designed to reject light from above while accepting light coming from below.

Standard or long-throw projector: Look for a long-throw ALR screen designed for the projector's position.

Lights on: ALR helps significantly with overhead or off-axis room lighting, but direct sunlight on the screen will still wash out the image.

Don't buy a UST ALR screen for a regular projector without checking compatibility.

For standard / long-throw projectors

A floor-rising ALR alternative for a projector placed farther back in the room. Check throw-distance requirements.

ALR performance depends on the projector angle and the direction of room lighting, not just the advertised light-rejection percentage.

The key is getting both the right screen material and the right mounting style. A normal white projector screen can look washed out in a bright room, even with an expensive projector.

## The important part: ALR isn't all the same

- **Ultra-short-throw (UST) projector:** Look for a *UST ALR / CLR* screen, designed to reject light from above while accepting light coming from below.
- **Standard or long-throw projector:** Look for a *long-throw ALR* screen designed for the projector's position.
- **Lights on:** ALR helps significantly with overhead or off-axis room lighting, but direct sunlight on the screen will still wash out the image.

Don't buy a UST ALR screen for a regular projector without checking compatibility.
